policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: Word-order variant only: both readings are the same three words, and ASV 'the third day' renders either order identically. Nothing in the English or in any note distinguishes them.
ASV opens the verse 'And Jesus saith unto her' with an unitalicized connective, rendering the conjunction that the omitting reading lacks.
The difference is word division/orthography only; both print the same relative expression, which ASV renders 'Whatsoever he saith unto you'. The English cannot distinguish them.
Word-order variant: 'waterpots of stone' translates either order, and English requires the noun before the material adjective regardless. No note bears on it.

Same words throughout; only the position of the participle differs. ASV 'set there after the Jews' manner of purifying' puts the participle first because English syntax requires it, not because it follows a Greek order, so the English does not distinguish the readings.

ASV 'And they bare it' has a connective, which both readings supply; ASV renders the postpositive connective and the coordinating conjunction alike as 'And'. The note here is classed alternative_rendering ('Or, steward') and concerns English wording only.
ASV renders 'and when men have drunk freely, then that which is worse' with 'then' unitalicized, i.e. not marked as an ASV supply, answering to the added adverb in this reading.
The variant adds only the article before 'beginning'. ASV 'This beginning of his signs' carries the demonstrative and leaves the article untranslated either way.
ASV 'his brethren' does not require the added pronoun: the Greek article is regularly rendered as a possessive in such a series, so the English leaves no distinct trace of the pronoun.
Singular against plural of the word for coin(s). ASV renders the collective mass noun 'the changers' money', which fits either number; no plural 'coins' shows through.
The two verbs differ by one letter and both mean to overturn; ASV 'overthrew their tables' renders either. No note bears on it.

ASV begins 'His disciples remembered' with no connective at all; the reading that adds a postpositive conjunction would have surfaced as one, since ASV renders such connectives rather than dropping them. The note here is a cross-reference (classed other) and does not bear on the reading.
Case variant of the relative pronoun. ASV 'the word which Jesus had said' renders either case with the same undeclined English relative.
The variant adds only the article before the name. ASV 'But Jesus did not trust himself' renders the proper name without an article either way.
All three readings are the reflexive object of the same verb, differing in breathing or in the full reflexive form; ASV 'did not trust himself unto them' renders any of them identically.
